name: Security Engineering for AI Agents
outcome: Threat-model and harden a bounded tool-using research agent, then verify its controls.
description: Assess trust boundaries, untrusted inputs, tool permissions, data exposure and failure containment in an existing AI application. Use a local sandbox and synthetic fixtures; focus on defensive verification.
learn: Identify trust boundaries and plausible agent failure modes
Restrict tools, validate inputs and enforce human approval for sensitive actions
Test security controls and record remaining risks
prior: Basic application security, HTTP and Python testing
practice: Harden the supplied two-tool research agent using synthetic inputs and dummy data in a local sandbox.
acceptance: Allowed tasks still work; disallowed tool calls are blocked; no sensitive data appears in logs; residual risks are documented.
external: Basic application security, HTTP and Python testing
moduleDescriptions: Map assets, untrusted data, permissions and sensitive actions.
Allowlist tools, validate arguments and separate instructions from data.
Use bounded execution and approval gates; protect secrets and research data.
Check that unsafe requests are rejected and document residual risks.
prerequisiteRationale: A06 provides experience implementing tool-using agents, so learners can reason about and verify actual application trust boundaries.
